title: Payroll Warrants and Direct Deposits— Fiscal Year 2021-2022 - July 1, 2021 - September 30, 2021 - Chief Business Officer
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Payroll Warrants and Direct Deposits - i.e., 3,021 Payroll Consolidated Checks printed and 24,009 Direct Deposits made - Fiscal Year 2020-2021, in the cumulative Amount of $67,260,334.53 from July 1, 2021 through September 30, 2021, as reflected in Exhibits 1-4.
headline: Approves $67.26M in payroll checks and direct deposits for July to September 2021
summary: The board approves the district's payroll payments for the first three months of the fiscal year: 3,021 printed checks and 24,009 direct deposits. The total is $67,260,334.53 for July 1 through September 30, 2021. Details are in Exhibits 1-4 attached to the item.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Accounts Payable Warrants - Fiscal Year 2021-2022 – July 1, 2021 - September 30, 2021 - Chief Business Officer
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Accounts Payable Warrants - i.e., 1651 Accounts Payable Consolidated Checks printed - Fiscal Year 2021-2022, in the cumulative Amount of $64,800,465.68 from July 1, 2021, through September 30, 2021, as reflected in Exhibits 1-4.
headline: Approves $64.8M in accounts payable checks issued July to September 2021
summary: The board approves the district's accounts payable payments (bills paid to vendors) for the first three months of the fiscal year. This covers 1,651 printed checks totaling $64,800,465.68 from July 1 through September 30, 2021. Details are in Exhibits 1-4 attached to the item.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
title: Agreement for Engineering Services – Jensen Hughes, Inc. – Hintil Kuu Child Development Center Fire & Intrusion Alarm Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Agreement for Engineering Services by and between the District and Jensen Hughes, Inc., Concord, California, for the latter to provide engineering and observation services including, but not limited to, preparation of a design to replace the existing fire alarm systems which includes site visits, review of the existing fire alarm system plans to develop the fire alarm system replacement design criteria, attend one pre-design meeting with the District to identify the fire alarm systems, and develop AutoCAD background drawings and site surveys, for the Hintil Kuu Child Development Center Fire & Intrusion Alarm Project, in the not-to-exceed amount of $101,700.00, which includes a contingency fee of $5,000.00, with work scheduled to commence on November 4, 2021, and scheduled to last until June 29, 2024, pursuant to the Agreement.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Hires Jensen Hughes for up to $101,700 to design a new fire alarm at Hintil Kuu Child Development Center
summary: Jensen Hughes, Inc. of Concord will design a replacement for the existing fire alarm systems at the Hintil Kuu Child Development Center, including site visits, a review of current plans and drawings and surveys. The limit of $101,700 includes a $5,000 contingency fee. Work is scheduled from November 4, 2021 to June 29, 2024.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
title: Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement –Viatron Systems, Inc. – Cole Administration Center Project – Division of Facilities Planning & Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement by and between the District and Viatron Systems, Inc., Gardena, CA, for the latter to provide additional services which includes manifesting all the files that were originally retrieved from the District’s storage space, creating a new database log of all the files, and organizing them in alphabetical order instead of the order they existed in the original physical file and as described in proposal attached to this amendment as part of Exhibit ”A.”, for the Cole Administration Center Project, in an additional amount of $37,628.20, increasing Agreement not-to-exceed amount from $308,795.00 to $346,423.20. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $37,628 to Viatron's contract to catalog and reorganize Cole Administration Center files
summary: This amendment gives Viatron Systems, Inc. extra work on the Cole Administration Center Project: listing all files retrieved from district storage, building a new database log of them and putting them in alphabetical order. It adds $37,628.20, raising the contract limit from $308,795.00 to $346,423.20. All other terms stay the same.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding - Oakland Reach - Chief Academic Officer
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding (“MOU”) by and between the District and Oakland REACH (“REACH”), defining the mutual obligations of the Parties, as stated in the MOU, more specifically Sections 3 and 4, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, in connection with the implementation of the REACH Programming and Partnership at Sojourner Truth Independent Study School, for the period July 21, 2021, through June 30, 2022,
headline: Ratifies a no-cost agreement with Oakland REACH for programming at Sojourner Truth school
summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Oakland REACH sets out each side's duties for REACH programming and partnership at Sojourner Truth Independent Study School. The item states no dollar amount. It covers July 21, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before this vote, so the board is approving it after the fact.
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (5–2), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Morgan Grace - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022, by and between the District and Morgan Grace, Antioch, CA, for the latter to work 1080 hours … to support teachers in the zoom classroom and the actual classroom with collaborating on activities that teach youth drug education, holistic health practices, how race, law, and politics influence rates of incarceration and exploitation of youth and other tasks, all as described in Exhibit A, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $32,400.00.
funding_source: TUPE - Youth Engagement Prop 56, TUPE Grade 6-12 Tier 2
headline: Ratifies up to $32,400 for a contractor to support drug and health education in classrooms
summary: An individual contractor will work up to 1,080 hours supporting teachers, in the Zoom and in-person classroom, on lessons about drug education, holistic health, and how race, law and politics affect youth incarceration and exploitation. Pay is capped at $32,400 for September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before this vote, so the board is approving it after the fact.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

schools: MLK Elementary School; Lafayette Elementary School

title: Sole Source Exception To Public Bidding - Services Agreement - Family Engagement Lab - Academics and Instruction Department
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0018 - Authorizing Use of Sole Source Exception To Public Bidding For Services Agreement With Family Engagement Lab and Approving a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between District and Family Engagement Lab, San Francisco, CA, to provide Text Messaging Services To Schools and Parents/Caregivers, As Specified Therein, for the period of August 2, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $200,000.00.
headline: Approves up to $200,000 for Family Engagement Lab text messaging, without public bidding
summary: The board approves a resolution allowing a sole source exception to public bidding (the district skips competitive bidding because it names one provider) and a services agreement with Family Engagement Lab. The company will provide text messaging services to schools and to parents and caregivers from August 2, 2021 through June 30, 2022, for up to $200,000.
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (6–1), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

title: Sole Source Exception To Public Bidding - Services Agreement - COVID-19 Support – Oakland Public Education Fund – Office of the Chief of Staff
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution 2122-0017 -  Authorizing Use Of Sole Source Exception To Public Bidding For Services Agreement With The Oakland Public Education Fund and Approving a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and the Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for COVID 19 Contact Tracing and Related Activates, As Specified Therein, for the period of August 15, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not-to-exceed $250,000.00.

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - School Services of California - Office of the Chief of Staff
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and School Services of California, Sacramento, CA, for the latter to work in a proactive manner to protect and advance the District's interest in Sacramento including developing strategies, monitoring legislation and budget items that would impact OUSD, and lobbying the Legislature and State Administration and perform other stated activities, all incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via the Office of the Chief of Staff, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $50,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for School Services of California to lobby in Sacramento for OUSD
summary: School Services of California will represent the district's interests in Sacramento, including developing strategies, monitoring legislation and budget items that affect OUSD, and lobbying the Legislature and State Administration. The cost is capped at $50,000 for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before this vote, so the board is approving it after the fact.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Joanna Kaplan, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide grant writing and management services including grant report writing, grant proposal writing, proposal editing, proposal and report research, document preparation, collaborative meetings for content development, planning, document review and gathering, and coordination of the grant submission process, via Office of the Chief of Staff, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $50,000.00.

title: Agreement for Architectural Services - Shah Kawasaki Architects - Coliseum Prep Academy at Havenscourt High School Site Expansion Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Agreement for Architectural Services by and between the District and Shah Kawasaki Architects, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide design services described in Articles 5 and 6 of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the design-build of Coliseum Prep Academy at Havenscourt High School Site Expansion Project, in the not to-exceed amount of $1,125,011.00, which includes a not-to-exceed amount of $100,000.00 for additional services, a not-to-exceed amount of $23,350.00 for reimbursable expenses, as the selected consultant, with work scheduled to commence on November 18, 2021, and scheduled to last until March 31, 2025.
